Road Rage

By: Busisiwe Gumede | Paid

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
Road rage, what makes some people more prone to anger behind the wheel?

Unique Selling Point:
Road rage is a massive problem internationally, especially in America. But experts are saying such incidents are increasing in the country. According to crime statistics, road rage is one of the top reasons you could be killed in mzansi. How widespread is this problem and what are its major contributors?

Summary:
Aggressive driving has become a topic of concern over the last few decades, and for good reason.

Further information:
During the presentation of the third-quarter figures for 2021-2022, it was revealed arguments and misunderstandings related to road rage and/or provocation, accounted for 1,151 murders.

There were also 1,215 attempted murder cases, including road rage incidents, along with 21,188 grievous bodily harm cases for the three months.

Johannesburg Metro Police Department spokesperson Wayne Minnaar said when a motorist committed a traffic offence such as skipping a red light, cutting off another motorist, overtaking when it was not safe, ignoring a stop sign, or reckless or negligent driving, it caused other motorists to react aggressively.

Script:


Alexandra township, Johannesburg...where many young people are unemployed and
while away time in the streets, idle.
So it’s encouraging when young people from here defy the odds...carve out a
promising future for themselves. At twenty one years old, Thando Khumalo was such a
man.

SOUND UP- SIPHO BOPHA
00:35 - 00:49 He was 20 and he had two businesses.


In his limited downtime, the hard-working young entrepreneur would hang out with
friends, but one night in October, a night of fun ended in tragedy for them - and Thando
became the latest victim in the country’s road rage epidemic.

PAUSE


After lockdown the country’s roads seem busier than ever - work commutes, traffic
jams - it’s a nightmare and ordinary people are exploding and unleashing
extraordinary violence.

In this video, a knife-wielding man attacks a Joburg motorist.
In another, a man brandishes a gun
Flaring tempers and weapons - a lethal cocktail

LINK THREE: Road rage is that uncontrollable feeling of wanting to plough your car
into another driver’s car. While the highway is no place for hot-tempered motorists, the
statistics indicate that road rage incidents are on the rise.
PAUSE

VO -
And that makes the road risky for all users...the 2022 crime statistics show that more
than 1 150 murders were caused by misunderstanding related to road rage and
provocation.

Bad driving habits increase frustration levels - like this woman, failing to indicators for
turning.
SOUND UP - https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=5Km2_4QOv0k

LADY DRIVER IN BAKKIE - 0.50 – Can you give me...(biker interjects) can you give me a
chance to pick a f>:*&”g lane before you swerve? (please check video for subtitle accuracy,
some parts not clear.)

3

PAUSE

VO – Trying to pinpoint the factors that contribute to car accidents, insurance company First
For Woman surveyed its customers.

Seugnette van Wyngaard says the findings show women are less inclined to initiate
physical, violent altercations - but they’re as prone to bad driving habits and road rage
as men.

SOUND UP- SEUGNETTE van WYNGAARD

03:32 – 03:50 - Like I said, 50% of the women admitted to driving too fast another, 25% said
they are aggressively hooting but yes the underlying factor is what’s contributing to road rage.
VO – With the holidays usually a stressful time on the roads, this year it follows a pandemic
with its economic pressures, and some motorists are anxious and easily triggered.
SOUND UP- SEUGNETTE van WYNGAARD

03:20 – 03:31 - Their experiences is really speaking about being stressed already, under
financial pressure, needing to get to work on time.

4

LINK ONE: Traffic delays, running late, the disregard for others and the law are some of
the common factors that often contribute to aggressive driving. But, what really drives
people to such levels of anger?

VO - Considering the factors underlying road rage, the expectation is that it will increase.

At the Anger and Stress Management Centre, Karen van Zyl has done extensive
research into the stress and anxiety that underlie road rage.

SOUND UP- KAREN VAN ZYL
01:33 - 01:42 - What I’ve come up with in my own investigation of this is stress and anxiety.
01:43 - 01:57 - So maybe the person is already pretty stressed and anxious and they get on
the road. Whether it’s financial or relationships or whatever and there’s sort of a proverbial
storm that breaks the camel's back.

VO – Impatience, feeling snubbed.. Hot tempers have many triggers.

SOUND UP- KAREN VAN ZYL

01:58 - 02:02 Other one that we’ve come up with as well is goal blocking. 02:03 - 02:15 When
somebody is driving and they perceive another driver is either obstructing their way that they
can’t get to where they want to get to.

VO – In the enclosed space of their cars, drivers may still feel safe and in control. Relatively
fewer incidents spill out into the street - but if the provocation is enough, drivers make
themselves vulnerable by stepping out and brandishing fists.
SOUND UP - https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=AZbrzaJkep8&t=404s

Man gets out of his car and walks to another car where a driver is seated inside..

DRIVER – 10.00 - I'm sorry for that (man slaps the driver for what?)

MAN - Sorry for what? You'll get beaten if you're a fool. Do you hear me?
VO – This man drove away from the encounter frazzled...possibly only his ego bruised.
But for young Thando Khumalo, the price was much higher on the night he went our
with his friends. His uncle, Sipho Bopha.

SOUND UP- SIPHO BOPHA

6

03:34 - 03:52 Usually what happens is whenever Thando and the friends go out they get a
driver to pick them up from home and then to wherever they’re going and then pick them up
and drop them home as a norm. So that’s what we know.

VO - Thando’s friends would later tell his uncle that a vehicle with four men almost collided
with theirs, so their driver stopped and confronted the four. That’s when things took a
turn for the worst.

SOUND UP- SIPHO BOPHA

06:36 - 06:51 One of Thando’s friends realised that actually these guys are carrying guns let’s
run. 06:52 - 07:10 The other guys ran away, Thando tried to run away as well.
VO – But the attackers were faster...

SOUND UP- SIPHO BOPHA

They caught up with him, beat him up, ... he got a good beating and then that’s when they
shot him at the back of the head.

PAUSE

VO- When his face appeared in social media, the man who allegedly shot Thando handed
himself over to the police. He’s appeared in court but awaits trial in prison.

Bopha says there is no evidence to suggest his nephew was killed for any reason other
than road rage.
SOUND UP- SIPHO BOPHA
03:02 - 03:18 It is road rage, it is road rage because I still don’t understand the reason you
would pull out a gun and shoot a child on the head, on top of that, beat the child up and shoot
him.

PAUSE

VO- He wants justice.
SOUND UP- SIPHO BOPHA
He knows what he did. He needs to take accountability and deal with it.

PAUSE – natsound from next scene

VO -“Taking responsibility” and getting people to reckon with themselves, has become
Hlanganani Wanda’s life mission after a 2008 road rage incident - that he caused -
nearly got him killed.
SOUND UP- HLANGANANI WANDA

02:45 - 02:54 From the time I was at home and leaving for work, I wasn’t ok. There were
some domestic issues. 02:55 – 03:03 So you know when something is troubling you and
you’re driving along the road I met up with traffic officers and they stopped me.

VO - Hlanganani was fined for not having his license with him.

SOUND UP- HLANGANANI WANDA

03:19 - 03:29 They gave me a ticket, just imagine after they gave me a ticket, I’m beginning to
run late as it’s 2:45pm and I start work at 3pm.
VO - As he was speeding to get to work on time, he narrowly avoided crashing into a
taxi.. the diver and passengers hurled insults at him.
SOUND UP- HLANGANANI WANDA

03:49 - 03:55 The taxi driver showed me the middle finger and I was annoyed. 03:58 - 04:09
In my annoyance, I thought, there’s already a knife in the car to keep myself safe. I was
driving behind him, I increased my speed and blocked him.

VO - So Hlangnanani climbed out of his car to teach the taxi man a lesson...
SOUND UP- HLANGANANI WANDA
04:18 ... With my knife in hand I went straight to him. 04:40 - 04:49 As I walked towards him,
he was those people that carried guns and put them on the side of the steering wheel. He
took out his gun, opened the door and (gestures)
VO - He’d realised he’d made a grave mistake.
SOUND UP- HLANGANANI WANDA
05:00 – 05:16 When he pointed the gun, I put my hands on my head and surrendered and my
knife fell. As I’m looking around and look at the passengers, they were laughing at me. 05:21
– 05:40 The driver was also laughing at me because now the knife has fallen and I’m no
longer a danger to him. He said “come take your knife, you’ll die one day.” [PAUSE] 04:18 -
04:29 I was annoyed and you know anger can drive you to do wrong things. ( Claire: it really
does)

9

PAUSE

REFLECTIVE LINK - What I realised as Hlanganani was speaking to me is
... He’s laughing not because it’s a funny situation but because perhaps
he’s embarrassed, he’s humiliated. ... And if it was any other situation any
other day then that would have turned out very differently for him. He
could have lost his life.

VO – There are ways a motorist can assess whether they’re heading toward road rage ..
ways to manage the anger before it explodes.
SOUND UP- SEUGNETTE van WYNGAARD
02:08 – 02:25 - ... there’s some basic questions that you can ask yourself to determine if you
are suffering from road rage. 02:27 – 02:42 - Questions like: Am I often speeding? Am I
excessively hooting? Am I cursing and swearing and shouting while I’m in traffic? Am I the
one cutting in front of someone else to try and teach them a lesson?

VO - Hlanganani knows he was very lucky that the taxi driver didn’t shoot him that day.
He now uses every opportunity to educate people not to repeat his mistake.
SOUND UP – HLANGANANI
09:25 - 09:40 If you take it to heart, you’re going to lose your family and your life. You see
cemeteries getting full, they are filled with people who weren’t thinking clearly because had
they used a cool head maybe it would be a better world.
